newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Press Digest - Ireland - January 17.
newsitem.headline: Press Digest - Ireland - January 17.

text.p: Following are the highlights of stories reported in the Irish press on Friday.

- The revenue commissioners are to bring tax evasion prosecutions against a number of "high-profile" people as part of a more aggressive policy which will involve a top team of 12 investigators who are being trained in England.
- Pressure for an early British election is mounting as Prime Minister John Major's majority finally slipped following the death of a Conservative MP.

- Allegations by an Israeli defence forces general that Irish peace-keeping troops sympathised with the Lebanese terror group Hizbullah were on Thursday night "rejected out of hand" by the Minister for Defence Sean Barrett.
- The Irish central bank is facing fresh worries over the currency after the punt fell below 98 pence against sterling on Thursday.
- Irish police have established clear links between INLA associates and some of the major drug dealing gangs in Dublin.
- Campaigners against the new national pay programme Partnership 2000 claimed on Thursday there was a growing tide of worker opposition to the deal which they say includes "meagre" increases.
- Irish airline travellers seem set to benefit from significantly reduced fares to a number of European cities.
- The Irish Stock Exchange expects to launch the new Developing Companies Market (DCM) within the next month despite on-going negotiations with the Department of Finance over tax incentives.
